questions.stem: What is the upward force acting on an object immersed in a fluid called?
questions.solution: The upward force acting on an object immersed in a fluid is called buoyant force. This force arises due to the pressure difference between the top and bottom of the object in the fluid. Gravitational force pulls objects downward, frictional force resists motion between surfaces, and magnetic force acts between magnetic materials, none of which apply in this context.

hi.stem: एक तरल में डूबे वस्तु पर ऊपर की ओर लगने वाला बल क्या कहलाता है?
hi.solution: एक तरल में डूबे वस्तु पर ऊपर की ओर लगने वाला बल उत्प्लावन बल कहलाता है। यह बल वस्तु के ऊपरी और निचले भाग पर दाब में अंतर के कारण उत्पन्न होता है। गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल वस्तु को नीचे की ओर खींचता है, घर्षण बल सतहों के बीच गति का विरोध करता है, और चुंबकीय बल चुंबकीय सामग्री के बीच कार्य करता है, इनमें से कोई भी इस संदर्भ में लागू नहीं होता।

questions.stem: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.solution: The SI unit of force is Newton. Dyne is a CGS unit, Joule is the unit of energy, and Pascal is the unit of pressure.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of the inertia of motion?
choices: A car suddenly stops and passengers lurch forward
A ball rolling on a flat surface comes to rest because it is pushed by friction
A book stays on a table unless moved
A person falls backward when a bus starts moving
questions.solution: The correct option is a car suddenly stopping and passengers lurching forward, which demonstrates inertia of motion because the passengers continue moving forward when the car stops. A ball coming to rest due to friction involves external forces, not inertia. A book staying on a table shows inertia of rest, not motion. A person falling backward when a bus starts is also inertia of rest, not motion.

questions.stem: If two forces of 10 N and 5 N are applied in opposite directions on an object, what is the net force acting on the object?
questions.solution: When two forces act in opposite directions, the net force is found by subtracting the smaller force from the larger one. Here, 10 N minus 5 N equals 5 N. The correct answer is 5 N. The other options incorrectly add the forces or use an incorrect calculation.

questions.stem: In an experiment, two bottles with magnets are placed in water and observed to move towards each other. What does this show?
choices: Magnetic force is a contact force
questions.solution: The bottles moving towards each other without touching shows a non-contact force is acting, as magnets can influence each other from a distance. Friction is a contact force and would require direct interaction, which is not observed. Balanced forces would mean no movement, contradicting the observed motion. Magnetic force is inherently a non-contact force, not a contact one.

hi.stem: एक प्रयोग में, दो बोतलों में चुंबक रखकर उन्हें पानी में रखा जाता है और देखा जाता है कि वे एक-दूसरे की ओर गति करते हैं। यह क्या दर्शाता है?

questions.stem: According to Archimedes’ Principle, what is the magnitude of the buoyant force equal to?
choices: The weight of the displaced fluid
questions.solution: According to Archimedes’ Principle, the buoyant force is equal to the weight of the fluid that is displaced by the object. This is because the force exerted by the fluid on the object is directly related to the amount of fluid pushed aside, not the object's own weight, density, or volume. The weight of the displaced fluid is the only quantity that directly determines the upward force acting on the object.
